metadata.title: Agents Swarm Orchestration - Sources
metadata.description: Official documentation, research, and secondary references for multi-agent orchestration across Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI Agents SDK

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Subagents Documentation
official_documentation.description: Official Claude Code guide for subagents, capabilities, mode-dependent background execution, worktree isolation, context forking, and nesting limits to check in the active runtime.

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Agent Teams Documentation
official_documentation.description: Official Claude Code guide for experimental agent teams, peer messaging, shared tasks, teammate limitations, automatic lifecycle, and cross-session messaging.

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Cross-Session Messaging
official_documentation.description: The agent-teams documentation also covers messaging independent Claude Code sessions without forming a team, including remote and platform-specific constraints.

official_documentation.name: Anthropic Claude Code Best Practices
official_documentation.description: Anthropic guidance for productive coding workflows, delegation, and context management

official_documentation.name: Codex Multi-Agents
official_documentation.description: Official Codex guidance for custom agents, main-thread ownership, parallel workers, read-heavy fan-out, and orchestration primitives

official_documentation.name: Codex Subagents
official_documentation.description: Official Codex configuration reference for custom-agent and concurrency settings; undocumented batch or nesting keys are not treated as portable contracts

official_documentation.name: OpenAI Agents SDK - Agents
official_documentation.description: Official Agents SDK documentation describing manager-style orchestration, handoffs, tools, and guardrails

official_documentation.name: OpenAI Agents SDK - Multi-Agent Guide
official_documentation.description: Official OpenAI multi-agent orchestration guide with code and design pattern examples

official_documentation.name: OpenAI Prompt Caching Guide
official_documentation.description: Official guide for structuring shared prompt prefixes and cache-friendly worker prompts

official_documentation.name: OpenAI Safety in Building Agents
official_documentation.description: Official safety guidance for prompt injection defense, structured outputs, approvals, and evals

official_documentation.name: OpenAI Models Overview
official_documentation.description: Current OpenAI model catalog for verifying latest flagship and smaller model options

official_documentation.name: Claude Code Workflows Documentation
official_documentation.description: Official reference for Dynamic Workflows: agent/parallel/pipeline primitives, concurrency ceilings, resume semantics

research.name: AdaptOrch: Task-Adaptive Multi-Agent Orchestration
research.description: Task-adaptive orchestration that maps decomposition shape to execution pattern instead of using one static topology

research.name: Latency-Aware Orchestration for Parallel Multi-Agent Systems
research.description: Accuracy and latency tradeoffs for parallel execution modeled over probabilistic DAGs

research.name: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Orchestration
research.description: Dynamic sequencing and prioritization with a learned orchestrator, useful as a design reference not a direct recipe

research.name: Aligned Agents, Biased Swarm: Measuring Bias Amplification in Multi-Agent Systems (Li et al., ICLR 2026)
research.description: Bias amplification observed in the experimental multi-agent systems studied; do not generalize to every pipeline.

research.name: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets (Tran & Kiela)
research.description: Apr 2026 arXiv preprint, NOT peer-reviewed; scope limited to multi-hop reasoning, text-only. Argues via the Data Processing Inequality that lossy handoffs cost information, favouring a single agent at equal budget; DPI does not imply every hop loses information. Basis for the equal-budget fan-out trap. Verify before relying.

research.name: Agent Contracts: A Formal Framework for Resource-Bounded Autonomous AI Systems (Ye & Tan)
research.description: Formal resource-bounded contracts and delegated budget conservation. This framework is not proof that a coding runtime enforces prompt-level budgets.

research.name: Antonio Gulli, Agentic Design Patterns (Springer, 2025) - Ch. 17 Reasoning Techniques
research.description: Publisher metadata and abstract confirm Antonio Gulli's Reasoning Techniques chapter (2025, pp. 241-263). The subscription-only chapter text was not read; attribution of this skill's graph record format and evidence rubric remains unverified. Treat those rules as repository design guidance, not claims from the chapter.

community_resources.name: claude-squad
community_resources.description: Terminal-based parallel Claude agent sessions; reference implementation for multi-agent concurrency patterns in local environments

community_resources.name: cmux
community_resources.description: Multiplexer for running multiple Claude agents in parallel; minimal orchestration approach for fan-out task execution

community_resources.name: figaro
community_resources.description: Desktop-based orchestration of Claude agent fleets; demonstrates local multi-agent coordination and session management

community_resources.name: gstack
community_resources.description: Claude Code configured as a virtual engineering team; reference for role-based agent orchestration and parallel workstreams

community_resources.name: LangGraph
community_resources.description: Agents-as-graphs framework with explicit state management; inspect the repository for its active API and support status before selecting it.

community_resources.name: Codex Multi Agent Playbook
community_resources.description: Secondary inspiration for Codex swarm workflows; useful for examples but should be checked against primary docs

community_resources.name: CODEX MULTI AGENT PLAYBOOK: SWARMS LVL. 1
community_resources.description: Long-form X Article on multi-agent swarm orchestration with Codex — covers Swarm Waves (sequential parallelism), Super Swarms (total parallelism), orchestrator roles, dependency graphs, max_threads config, and model/reasoning level selection per agent

community_resources.name: Nav Toor — 30 Claude Code Sub-Agents I Actually Use
community_resources.description: Practitioner prompt catalog, cited as inspiration for named worker self-rejection criteria; popularity figures and effectiveness are unverified.

community_resources.name: Claude Subagents vs. Agent Teams, Explained
community_resources.description: Explainer on two distinct multi-agent paradigms in Claude Code: when to use subagents (isolated context, delegation) vs. agent teams (collaborative, shared context). Key insight: most people reach for multi-agent when they shouldn't

community_resources.name: The Machine that Builds the Machine — Symphony
community_resources.description: Secondary discussion of issue-driven agent orchestration. Operational figures are unverified here; use the primary implementation and measured runs before quoting results.

community_resources.name: Andrej Karpathy - Claude Coding Notes
community_resources.description: Operator-level coding-agent pitfalls that justify verifier loops, tighter scope control, and resistance to overcomplicated multi-agent execution

community_resources.name: Sarah Chieng - Lessons Learned From Building Multi-Agent Workflows
community_resources.description: April 2026 field report on orchestrator-plus-line-cook patterns, minimum viable context, phased fan-out, no shared-file writes, and one-builder-plus-verifiers discipline

community_resources.name: Walden Yan - Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working
community_resources.description: April 2026 Cognition update: parallel-writer swarms still fail in practice; the narrow class that works is manager-and-workers setups where extra agents contribute intelligence while writes stay single-threaded

community_resources.name: Claude Code Agents In 2026: Agent View, Subagents, Teams, And What Parallel Sessions Actually Cost
community_resources.description: Secondary cost analysis; numerical savings are unverified here. Calculate costs from current provider prices and measured usage.

community_resources.name: Agentic AI Frameworks 2026: LangGraph vs CrewAI vs OpenAI SDK
community_resources.description: Secondary framework comparison; verify release status and APIs against each framework's official documentation before selection.

community_resources.name: Multi-Agent in Production 2026: 3 Patterns That Survived
community_resources.description: May 2026 production survey describing orchestrator-worker as the default multi-agent pattern in production, alongside supervisor/hierarchical and swarm (peer, no central control) as the other two topologies that survived. The page does not state a specific adoption percentage — do not cite a numeric split from this source.

community_resources.name: Claude Code Workflows: Deterministic Multi-Agent Orchestration (alexop.dev)
community_resources.description: Walkthrough of script-held control flow, barrier-vs-pipeline tradeoffs, and context-cost rationale

community_resources.name: The Workflow Tool: Scripted Multi-Agent Orchestration (ClaudeWorld)
community_resources.description: Tutorial on workflow scripts: primitives, structured output schemas, and determinism constraints

community_resources.name: The Parallel Subagent Race: Codex CLI Multi-Agent v2 vs Claude Dynamic Workflows
community_resources.description: Side-by-side comparison of Codex declarative TOML roles vs Claude Code code-mode orchestration; depth and thread defaults

community_resources.name: Graphs vs. Loops: Agentic AI Orchestration Debate 2026 (explainx.ai)
community_resources.description: July 2026 industry debate framing graph-structured vs loop-structured agent orchestration

community_resources.name: Bun: Rewriting Bun in Rust (Zig-to-Rust port case study)
community_resources.description: Primary migration account; read it before quoting figures. A case study does not establish a portable concurrency limit or correctness guarantee.

community_resources.name: The Register: Zig creator calls Bun's Claude Rust rewrite 'unreviewed slop'
community_resources.description: Secondary critique of migration review debt; reported regression counts are unverified here.

community_resources.name: cursor pstack plugin (MIT)
community_resources.description: MIT-licensed external plugin. Accessed 2026-09-29. Informed the delegate-result-hygiene rule (drop/rerun on missing commit-or-tree-state and method; never resume an interrupted worker with changed scope), the qa-test-reviewer vacuous-test pre-check, and the hill-climbing loop guardrails (one change per measurement, freeze a sensitivity-verified harness, stop on stated target plus minimum attempts, decision logging). Rules adapted and rewritten in this repository's own words; no text copied verbatim.
